Headline results for run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20, 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, covering 3.314% of the time):

- Records analysed: 759
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
- Catalogue (LBNL/NCEDC, GDR 859, March 2016): 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated estimate, using the LBNL catalogue):
  b=1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(Mw>=5.5) per observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(Mw>=3)/yr = 0.03719
  b=0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922,  P(Mw>=5.5) per observed volume = 0.0002155, P(Mw>=3)/yr = 0.2809
  b=0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474,   P(Mw>=5.5) per observed volume = 0.0006484, P(Mw>=3)/yr = 0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated magnitudes; every DAS detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated catalogue-based probabilities of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event are very low (1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 per year depending on the b scenario), while the DAS-based upper bound (0.0784/yr) is much higher because the DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and all 62 detections are treated as events at/above Mc, so it over-counts. The calibrated estimate is the LBNL-catalogue-based one; the DAS-based number is the upper bound.
